skills.name: Variables and assignment
skills.description: A variable holds its latest value; the right-hand side is evaluated first.

skills.name: Tracing assignments
skills.description: Copying values between variables; why a naive swap fails.

CS_KEEPS_FIRST.label: Thinks a variable keeps its first value
CS_KEEPS_FIRST.explanation: Predicts that after x = 3 then x = 7, x is still 3.

CS_ASSIGN_LINK.label: Thinks `b = a` links the two variables forever
CS_ASSIGN_LINK.explanation: Predicts that changing a later also changes b.

CS_SWAP.label: Thinks `a = b` followed by `b = a` swaps two values
CS_SWAP.explanation: Misses that the first assignment overwrites a's old value.

hints: A variable is a labelled box holding ONE value at a time.
A new assignment replaces the old value.
solution: x starts as 3.
x = 7 replaces it, so x is 7.
The program prints 7.

solution: x starts as 4.

That result is stored back in x, so it prints 9.

variable_assignment.title: Variables and assignment
variable_assignment.big_idea: A variable is like a labelled box that holds one value at a time. `x = 7` puts 7 in the box and throws away whatever was there before.
steps: Work out the right-hand side first, using the CURRENT values.
Store the result in the variable on the left, replacing the old value.
Only the latest value is kept.
variable_assignment.sense_check: `x = x + 1` would be impossible in maths, but in code it just means: x gets (old x) + 1.

variable_tracing.title: Tracing assignments step by step
variable_tracing.big_idea: `b = a` copies a's value into b at that moment. The two variables are not linked, so changing one later does not change the other.
steps: Make a trace table with one column per variable.
Go line by line and update only the variable on the left of `=`.
When a value is overwritten, cross it out: it is gone.
At print, read the current values from the table.
variable_tracing.sense_check: To swap two cups of juice you need a third, empty cup. Code needs a temporary variable too.
